solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Supposing that infiltrating US agent was like a whistle-blower?

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the words for supposing go into the agent

parts.note: a Fed is an FBI agent in American slang
if means supposing that

explanation.surface: A spy story: a hypothetical agent working undercover turns out to be a whistle-blower.
explanation.walkthrough: The whistle-blower is not an informer but someone blowing a small whistle-like instrument, the fife.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a fife, a small flute, is literally to blow a kind of whistle.

clue.text: A few rising in garrison will be top-ranked

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the garrison

parts.note: a fort is a garrisoned stronghold

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: some means a few

explanation.surface: A handful of soldiers climbing the ranks within the garrison will reach the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading or chief, first in rank or importance.

clue.text: Fish swimming round capital are reddish-purple

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the scrambled fish letters wrap around the capital
swimming suggests moving about, so the letters of fish are rearranged

parts.note: UC is upper case, capital letters
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Fish circling a city look reddish-purple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is not a city but upper case, UC; 'are' is the unit of area, A.
explanation.definitionFit: The shade takes its name from the fuchsia plant's vivid purplish-red flowers.

clue.text: Lose heart in dull work assignment

indicators.note: lose heart in asks for the middle letter of the word for dull to be removed

parts.note: dusty means dull and dry, as a dusty lecture

explanation.surface: A boring task makes a worker lose heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A task or shift one is assigned, as being on duty.

clue.text: Fish to fill a hulk at sea, or pass under it?

indicators.note: to fill means to go into, so the fish goes inside the scrambled letters
at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A nautical scene: stuffing fish into an old ship, or perhaps sailing beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges A HULK into KHAUL, which 'to fill' opens to take EEL. The definition's 'it' is the hulk: the old punishment dragged a sailor under a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval punishment dragged an offender beneath a vessel's bottom from one side to the other.

clue.text: Barbarian occupiers smite opposition to Federation

indicators.note: barbarian suggests savage disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Savage invaders strike down those resisting a federated empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility to closer union of the European Union, seen by critics as a federal superstate.

clue.text: Sign of growth heading off reversal of boom

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: the opposite of an economic boom is a slump

explanation.surface: An economist sees a sign of growth fending off a downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversal' is not a backwards reading: it means the opposite of a boom.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelling or bump may show a tumour or other growth on the body.

clue.text: Plants spies among industrial relations group

indicators.note: among puts the spies inside the group

parts.note: ACAS is the UK Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, which settles workplace disputes
the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: Undercover agents are planted inside a labour arbitration body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plants' looks like the moles in the surface, but it is the definition: the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattles and thorn trees of the genus Acacia are plants.

clue.text: Left for dead in stratagem's retreat

indicators.note: for means instead of, so one letter replaces the other

parts.note: a dodge is a stratagem or trick

explanation.surface: A soldier is left for dead during a strategic withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin or hunting lodge is a remote retreat.

clue.text: Two with heavy habits wasted benefit from incompatible situations

indicators.note: wasted means wrecked or ruined, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair with bad addictions are left wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a joining word; the fodder is TWO, HEAVY and HABITS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for enjoying the advantages of two contradictory positions at once.

clue.text: Filling for some pasta or apricot tart

definitions.text: Filling for some pasta or apricot tart

indicators.note: the filling of the words apricot tart is the run of letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A cook lists what might go inside ravioli or a fruit tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling' works twice: the cheese fills pasta, and it is the filling of the phrase 'apricot tart'.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft Italian cheese is a standard stuffing for ravioli and cannelloni and also goes into baked tarts.

clue.text: Border with unopened flower enthrals a poet

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge

indicators.note: enthrals means holds captive, so the flower holds the letter a inside it

parts.note: a bud is a flower not yet opened

explanation.surface: An edging of budding blooms captivates a passing poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Rimbaud was a nineteenth-century French poet, author of A Season in Hell.

clue.text: Movers and shakers' leading couples dance boisterously

indicators.note: leading couples asks for the first pair of letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: The influential people are seen leading couples onto the floor in a lively dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading couples' takes the first two letters of each word, MO and SH, not one letter apiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Moshing is the rough, jostling dancing of a crowd at a rock or punk gig.

clue.text: Break off end of chocolate in box

indicators.note: in places the final letter inside the box

parts.note: a case is a box

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of chocolate

explanation.surface: Someone snaps off the end of a chocolate bar kept in its box.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop or halt something is to break it off, as talks or fighting.

clue.text: Dismiss feminine fury

parts.note: F is the grammatical abbreviation for feminine
ire is fury or anger

explanation.surface: A woman's rage is waved away as unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack or let go an employee is to dismiss them from a job.

clue.text: Limit uranium in atomic force

indicators.note: in puts the uranium symbol inside the force

parts.note: a chemical bond is a force holding atoms together
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A cap is placed on uranium in nuclear forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound is a limit or boundary, as in out of bounds.

clue.text: Conservationist's note after consent initially withheld

indicators.note: after places the note following the cut word
initially withheld means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to agree is to consent

explanation.surface: An environmentalist's memo arrives after permission was at first denied.
explanation.definitionFit: Environmental politics and its supporters are described with this colour, as the Green Party.

clue.text: Petty officer in inclination to cut stir, adapting trivial punishment

indicators.note: in puts the officer inside the word for inclination

parts.note: a slant is an inclination or tilt
PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

indicators.note: adapting means altering, so the letters of stir are rearranged

explanation.surface: A petty officer, inclined to cut short trouble on board, adapts a mild penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' looks like prison slang but is just letters: 'adapting' rearranges them to RIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A token rebuke, mild discipline for an offence, is figuratively a light smack on the arm.

clue.text: The object in a vegetable expedition

indicators.note: in places the pronoun inside the vegetable

parts.note: celery is a vegetable
it is the object pronoun, the object in a sentence

explanation.surface: An item found inside a vegetable on a field trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' looks like a journey, but it is its older sense, speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed, matching swiftness.

clue.text: Plummy addition (possibly kitchen coinage)

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of the two words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A rich extra, perhaps money stashed in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plummy' looks like it means posh-voiced, but here it is 'excellent, desirable', as in a plum job.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a pleasing extra that tops off something already good, like the sugary layer on a fruit cake.

clue.text: One splits first element installed in boiler

indicators.note: installed in means fitted inside, so the element letter goes into the boiler

parts.note: a copper is an old British laundry boiler
hydrogen, symbol H, is the first element of the periodic table

explanation.surface: A plumber fits the first heating element into a boiler that cracks.
explanation.definitionFit: An axe or cleaver is a tool for splitting wood or meat.

clue.text: When transforming, a coil is avoiding contact

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left

indicators.note: transforming means changing form, so the letters of a coil are rearranged

explanation.surface: An electrical coil being transformed keeps clear of any contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unsociable shuns company and avoids mixing with others.

clue.text: Turn page in boozer

indicators.note: in puts the page letter inside the drunkard

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard, a boozer

explanation.surface: A page boy takes a turn in the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' suggests a British pub, but here it is the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's slot or act in a show is a turn, such as a comedy spot.

clue.text: Places turned over when European enters organisation

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so the European letter goes inside
turned over means reversed, so the word for places is read backwards

parts.note: puts means places

explanation.surface: Seats are overturned when a European joins the organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The way something is arranged or structured is its setup.

clue.text: Control constant blazes

parts.note: C is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
blazes and heck are both mild oaths, as in what the blazes

explanation.surface: Firefighters keep a steady hold over ongoing fires.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain or keep something in check is to control it.

clue.text: See in Tom, Dick or Harry a god

indicators.note: in places the letter for see inside the ordinary fellow

parts.note: Joe is any ordinary man, as in Joe Bloggs
V stands for vide, Latin for see, in references

explanation.surface: Spotting a deity inside an everyday bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter, chief of the Roman gods, is also known by this poetic name.

clue.text: Female with very mature bust

parts.note: old means very mature in years

explanation.surface: A description of an older woman's figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a noun for the chest, but it is the verb: go bust.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that collapses or goes broke is said to fold.

clue.text: Wag needing Jag, say, and diamonds

parts.note: a Jag, a Jaguar, is an example of a car
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: A show-off who needs a Jaguar and jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker or comic person is called a card or a wag.

clue.text: Pak choi is plant regularly cut up for root starch

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards
regularly cut means every other letter is removed, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A recipe: chop up an Asian green to make a starchy root dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly cut' keeps the even letters ACOIPAT; 'up' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: This starch comes from the cassava root and is used for puddings and thickening.

clue.text: Small complaint before one grasps hard African language

indicators.note: grasps means holds, so the letters for small, complaint and one hold the letter for hard

parts.note: a wail is a cry of complaint
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A minor gripe comes before someone gets a firm grip.
explanation.definitionFit: This Bantu tongue is widely spoken across East Africa, in Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Public address wicked lives with ecstasy or bliss

parts.note: wicked and rad are both slang for excellent
is means lives or exists
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An announcer's loudspeaker praises an evil lifestyle of drugs and pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' looks like evil, but it is the slang 'great', giving RAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven, or any state of perfect happiness, is complete bliss.

clue.text: Line incorporated by act towards sound system

parts.note: to do is to act
by can mean towards, as in by evening

explanation.surface: A line in a play is written into an act heading for the speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolby is a trademark noise-reduction and surround audio technology used in cinemas.
